questions.question: What does an index do in a database?

options.text: Stores data in a random fashion.

questions.explanation: Indexes are data structures that improve the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table.

questions.question: What is the purpose of partitioning in databases?

options.text: To split a table into smaller, manageable pieces.

questions.explanation: Partitioning helps in managing large tables by dividing them into smaller, more manageable pieces.

questions.question: Caching can improve query performance.
questions.explanation: Caching stores the results of expensive queries, allowing faster retrieval on subsequent requests.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of indexing?
questions.explanation: Indexes do not increase data redundancy; they improve query performance and data retrieval speed.

questions.question: Partitioning always improves performance.
questions.explanation: While partitioning can enhance performance, it may not always be the best solution depending on the workload and query patterns.
